speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to my office. I understand you have swelling in your right knee and a family history of similar issues; to begin our assessment, how old are you and exactly how long has this swelling been present? Additionally, does the knee pain worsen with activity or occur even at rest?

speaker: Patient
text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis (specifically Polyarticular Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis) is less likely given the isolated presentation and lack of fever, but Osgood-Schlatter disease or a bone tumor must be ruled out. Given the age, onset after activity, and family history of similar issues, I need to clarify the nature of the "similar problems" in the uncle's family and perform a physical exam. REQUEST TEST: CBC, ESR, CRP. REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray of the right knee.
